claims.explanation: Bergenin's anti-inflammatory activity via NF-κB/MAPK inhibition and PPARγ agonism likely sensitizes lines with high basal NF-κB/IL-1/TNF signaling or oxidative-stress dependence, while protective features include intact KEAP1/NRF2 antioxidant response and PTEN loss with PI3K/AKT-driven survival. The selective killing pattern is best explained by lineage-independent dependence on inflammatory/NF-κB and redox pathways rather than a single driver mutation.

features.basis: NRF2 pathway addiction may increase dependence on antioxidant response that bergenin disrupts
KEAP1 loss constitutively activates NRF2 antioxidant program, countering bergenin-induced oxidative stress
PTEN loss enhances PI3K/AKT survival signaling, reducing sensitivity to anti-inflammatory/oxidative stress agents
TP53-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting impaired DNA damage/apoptotic response
BRAF-mutant melanoma and thyroid lines appear in sensitive set, possibly via MAPK dependence
EGFR-mutant lung and glioma lines are enriched in sensitive set, linking RTK signaling to NF-κB activation
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and ovarian lines appear in both sets but KRAS-driven survival may buffer NF-κB inhibition
High IL-1β signaling creates NF-κB dependence that bergenin inhibits
TNF-driven NF-κB activation is suppressed by bergenin, so high TNF expression predicts sensitivity
Bergenin acts as PPARγ agonist; high PPARγ expression may mediate anti-inflammatory effects
Bergenin improves SIRT1 expression, inhibiting NF-κB; low SIRT1 may reduce response
SMARCA4-mutant lines appear in sensitive set, possibly via chromatin remodeling affecting NF-κB targets
